children: Crude oil contracts fell more than $3 around midday Wednesday, largely giving back the previous day's significant gain, driven by wider threats on Middle East shipping routes and energy infrastructure.
At 12:10 p.m. ET, more-active November Nymex WTI was down $3.30 to around $97.45/bbl and October WTI was $3.45 lower to $102.35/bbl.
London-based November ICE Brent was down by about $3.30 to $105.35/bbl, and December Brent was $2.85 lower to $100.45/bbl.

Diesel futures also retreated sharply following Tuesday's strong rally. November ULSD was 2.25cts lower to $4.9875/gal and October ULSD was down 4.65cts to $5.2155/gal. November RBOB was 3.85cts lower to $3.208/gal and October RBOB was down 2.10cts to $3.4445/gal.

The energy market is digesting the latest weekly data from the Energy Information Administration, which showed increases in both gasoline and distillate inventories for the week ended Friday. However, U.S. commercial crude oil stocks were down during the period.
